newsitem.title: USA: No word yet on Pakistan wheat tender - U.S. trade.
newsitem.headline: No word yet on Pakistan wheat tender - U.S. trade.

text.p: U.S. exporters said awards in Pakistan's tender for 500,000 tonnes of wheat were expected overnight with U.S. origin-grain possibly taking half the amount or slightly more.
A senior U.S. wheat export trader said the maximum amount of wheat Pakistan could buy with its remaining GSM-102 U.S. government financing was 225,000 tonnes.
"Pakistan may get some private financing and could buy more U.S. wheat," the exporter said.
Pakistan seeks 500,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat for August 11-September 10 shipment. An official at Pakistan's embassy in Washington D.C. said awards would come out Tuesday.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture last week raised by $25 million the amount of GSM-102 credit guarantees available for sale of U.S. farm goods to Pakistan, boosting Pakistan's 1997 (Oct/Sept) fiscal year allocation to $325 million.
U.S. traders said Pakistan was expected to buy wheat from the United States, Australia and Canada.
"The Australian prices are in the range of $158 to $159. I do not know how many tonnes," a second senior wheat export trader said late on Monday.
"I don't know the total quantity," the first exporter said, referring to Australia's offer. "There was plenty of wheat offered, about 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes at $158."
Canada was offering $147.50, FOB, Pacific ports, for about 50,000 tonnes, the exporter said.
The second exporter said U.S. firms were being pretty tight-lipped about their offers "because they think they have offered the U.S. wheat pretty cheap."
"I heard the price range was $148.22 up to $149.43, FOB, Pacific Northwest," for about 200,000 tonnes of U.S. white wheat, the first exporter said.
He believed ther was another 100,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat on offer at between $149.87 and $150.05. "They definitely would not buy more than 300,000 tonnes U.S. wheat," the trader said.
